# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

Ashirwad Scheme (Shagun for Daughter's Marriage)
Department of Social Justice, Empowerment & Minorities, Punjab

It was earlier called the Shagun scheme. Since 28 January 2026 applications are taken only at Sewa Kendras, before the wedding or within 60 days after it, and the money goes straight to the bank account.

Lado Protsahan Yojana (Lado Sankalp Patra)
Directorate of Women Empowerment, Women & Child Development Department, Government of Rajasthan

A girl born in a government hospital or a JSY-approved private hospital in Rajasthan is promised Rs 1.5 lakh, paid in seven instalments from birth until she graduates at 21. Mukhyamantri Matritva Poshan Yojana (MMMPY)
Directorate of Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), Women & Child Development Department, Government of Rajasthan

Gives Rs 6,000 in three instalments to a woman pregnant with her second child, for better food and care. It was earlier called the Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana; only the name changed and the rules are the same. If the second baby is a boy, the third instalment is Rs 4,000; if it is a girl, she gets Rs 6,000 under the central PM Matru Vandana Yojana instead, making Rs 8,000 in all. There is no form: the Anganwadi worker or ANM records the pregnancy on PCTS and the money comes by DBT.
Rs 6,000 in 3 instalments for the second child (Rs 8,000 in all if it is a girl)

Runs in all districts; pregnant or breastfeeding Anganwadi workers, helpers, ASHA sahyoginis and saathins are also eligible
Not for women regularly employed by the Centre, the state or a PSU, or getting the same kind of benefit under another law
Not eligible if the first pregnancy gave twins, or if after remarriage either partner already has more than one child

Mukhyamantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (Rajasthan top-up to PM-Kisan)
Agriculture Department, Government of Rajasthan

Rajasthan adds its own money to PM-Kisan. Every Rajasthan farmer family that receives PM-Kisan also gets Rs 3,000 a year from the state, paid in instalments of Rs 1,000, so the total becomes Rs 9,000 a year with the Centre's Rs 6,000. There is no separate state form: a farmer registered and active in PM-Kisan gets the state money by DBT automatically.
Rs 3,000 a year from the state on top of PM-Kisan's Rs 6,000 (Rs 9,000 in all)
